Keep Your Lamborghini Revuelto and Sign Us Up for This Aventador SVJ Roadster Instead
12 photos
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago
There’s an entirely new supercar king in Lamborghini’s portfolio, and it’s not the Fenomeno . The latter is part of the brand’s few-off series, for whatever reason, it does not get that much attention. But its mainstream sibling, the Revuelto, does.
More often than not, a few examples of this model end up in our news feed weekly. Either due to a tuning job or the used car market. But this story has nothing to do with the Revuelto, but its predecessor, the Aventador. Made between 2011 and 2022, it gave birth to some extremely cool models, including the Veneno, Centenario, Essenza SCV12, Countach LPI 800-4, and Sian FKP 37, as well as the two Alston models, the SC18 and SC20.
On top of these, the Lamborghini Aventador was offered in the LP 700-4, SuperVeloce LP 750-4, S LP 740-4, SVJ LP 770-4, SVJ, and LP 780-4 Ultimae, among others. Ask any Lambo fan what their favorite Aventador is, and you will get different answers, though most of the time, petrolheads will mention the Super Veloce Jota (SVJ). This model debuted at the Pebble Beach Concours d’Elegance back in 2018, boasting several improvements over the S and the SV.
It is a track-focused model and the first V12 Lambo to boast the ALA (Aerodinamica Lamborghini Attiva), so the aero upgrades were on deck, including the disconnected front splitter, a big carbon fiber rear wing with a central fin, a tri-dimensional air outlet on the hood, a large rear diffuser, and underbody vortex generators. The LDVA 2.0 (Lamborghini Dinamica Veicolo Attiva) management system is also on deck, thus further contributing to the car’s track-enhanced nature, and making it faster overall.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago The Lamborghini Aventador SVJ Roadster followed its fixed-roof sibling, being presented to the world at the 2019 Geneva Motor Show (the good old days!). It featured the same goodies, albeit with an open-top view of the sky above, consisting of a removable two-piece carbon fiber hard top. And if you dream about owning one of these, then you should know that the example shown in the gallery is looking for a new home in the United States of America.
This Italian supercar features a Grigio Liqueo exterior on top of a Nero Cosmus and Bianco Polar interior, and at the time of cataloging, it had in the region of 2,000 miles (3,200 km) on the clock. Thus, you are looking at an almost-new machine, despite being a 2020 model, and as you likely suspect, there isn’t anything wrong with it, as everything looks good, from the black Y-spoke alloys and green details, to the black leather and Alcantara upholstery, and the white contrasting elements on the inside.
You do know how much the Lamborghini Aventador SVJ Roadster unleashes at a hard push of the right pedal, don’t you? That would be 759 bhp (770 ps/566 kW) and 531 lb-ft (720 Nm) of torque, with the maximum thrust available at 6,750 rpm, and the peak output at 8,500 rpm. The 6.5-liter naturally aspirated V12 engine is mounted behind the passenger compartment, and works in concert with a 7-speed ISR, and a gen-4 Haldex all-wheel drive system.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago Despite its open-top nature, it is just as fast from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) as its fixed-roof sibling, as the acceleration takes 2.8 seconds. This makes it 0.3 seconds slower than the Revuelto, which uses a plug-in hybrid 6.5L naturally aspirated V12, with 1,001 hp (1,015 ps/747 kW) in total. The new Revuelto SV has 1,050 hp (1,065 ps/783 kW) to play with, and is 0.1 seconds faster than the standard Revuelto. As for the smaller Temerario, it hits 62 mph in 2.7 seconds, and has an electrified 4-liter twin-turbo V8 with 789 hp (800 ps/588 kW) in total.
Now, if you dream about owning a Lamborghini Aventador SVJ, then your pockets must be really deep, because this thing is on the extremely expensive side of things, regardless of the body style. For instance, the Roadster , which is the configuration of the pictured supercar, will set you back a minimum of $1.2 million in today’s market in the United States of America, and can easily exceed $1.5 million. Ultra-low mileage examples with less than 2,000 miles on the clock push past $1.6 million.
So, how much is the pictured Lamborghini Aventador SVJ Roadster? Unless you said $1,599,995, then you are wrong, because this was the asking price of the said supercar at the time of writing. You can find it in the possession of @motorcarsofchicago on Instagram, with the dealer stating that it accepts trade-ins and offers financing, and is not really fond of direct messages.
Thus, there you have it folks, if you have a $1.6-million budget and the desire to get one of these , then you know where you can find this supercar. By the way, a regular Lamborghini Revuelto will set you back over $610,000 new. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Motor Cars of Chicago (@motorcarsofchicago)
